caption:
What a stray looks like is already decided.

Southwest Research Institute wrote it into a release. Strays "appear to be malnourished and skittish". Dogs that seem healthier and more approachable "are likely owned by local families and are classified as roaming."

In San Antonio the call now starts with a phone mounted on a vehicle window. Object detection software finds the dogs. Automated and human review checks each call.

The project repeats a 2019 manual survey in the same 32 study areas. It isn't meant to count every dog.

A final report goes to Animal Care Services. Director Jon Gary calls the study another tool for seeing where loose dogs turn up.

The deck follows one dog from a car window to a reviewer's screen.

Will the report SwRI sends after December say how often a person overruled the software's stray call?
